newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds lower on interbank rate.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended lower across the board in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Monday.
"Bond prices were marked down slightly again following another small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.73/98.78 compared with last Friday's close of S$98.85/98.90, September 2001 at S$97.55/97.60 against S$97.80/97.85 and June 2003 at S$95.55/95.60 from S$95.80/95.85.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent versus last Friday's 2 1-7/8 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.25/1.20 percent against last Friday's yield of 1.03/0.98 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.75/1.70 percent from 1.68/1.63 percent.
